name: CISSP Domain 6 – Security Assessment and Testing

questions.stem: Which type of test gives the tester full knowledge of source code, architecture, and credentials before testing begins?
questions.explanation: White-box (clear-box) testing provides full internal knowledge. Black-box gives none, and blind/double-blind describe what the tester or defenders know about the engagement.

questions.stem: Before starting a penetration test of a production network, what must a consultant obtain FIRST?
options: Written authorization defining scope and rules of engagement
A copy of the incident response plan
questions.explanation: Written, signed authorization with scope and rules of engagement is the legal and ethical prerequisite. Without it testing may be illegal; the other items are optional inputs.

questions.stem: A SOC 2 Type II report differs from a Type I report primarily because it:
options: Evaluates operating effectiveness of controls over a period of time
questions.explanation: Type II tests operating effectiveness over a period (typically 6-12 months); Type I covers design at a point in time. SOC 1 addresses financial reporting, and SOC 3 is the public report.

questions.stem: A company wants to share assurance about its cloud service's security controls with prospects on its public website. Which report is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: SOC 3 is a general-use summary suitable for public distribution. SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports are restricted-use, and ISAE 3402 addresses financial reporting controls.

questions.stem: Which testing technique feeds malformed, random, or unexpected input to an application to find crashes and input-handling flaws?
questions.explanation: Fuzzing supplies invalid or random input to dynamically uncover robustness flaws. Static analysis doesn't execute code, regression testing confirms changes didn't break function, and misuse cases are design artifacts.

questions.stem: A vulnerability scan reports a critical flaw on a server, but manual review shows the vulnerable package was backported with a patch. This result is BEST described as a:
questions.explanation: The scanner flagged a vulnerability that doesn't exist, which is a false positive, common with version-banner checks on backported packages. A false negative would be a missed real flaw.

questions.stem: To reduce false positives and get more accurate patch-level findings from vulnerability scans, what should a security team do?
options: Scan only from outside the firewall
Switch to passive network monitoring only
questions.explanation: Authenticated scans inspect installed packages and configurations directly, improving accuracy. More frequent or external-only scans don't fix the underlying inference problem, and passive monitoring has less visibility.

questions.stem: Which code review method examines source code without executing it?
questions.explanation: SAST analyzes source or binaries without running them. DAST and fuzzing exercise the running application, and synthetic transactions monitor live behavior.

questions.stem: An organization runs scripted transactions every five minutes against its e-commerce site to verify availability and response time. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Synthetic monitoring uses scripted, simulated transactions to proactively test functionality and performance. Real user monitoring passively observes actual user sessions.

questions.stem: An auditor finds that the security team selects which logs to review based on alert volume, and many systems are never reviewed. What should the CISO do FIRST?
options: Define a risk-based log management policy establishing what must be collected and reviewed
Increase log retention to seven years
questions.explanation: Policy and risk-based requirements must come first to guide what is collected, reviewed, and retained. Tools and retention changes follow governance; disabling logs reduces visibility.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of clipping levels in audit log review?
options: Set a threshold below which routine events are not flagged for review
questions.explanation: Clipping levels are baselines so only activity exceeding a threshold (e.g., more than three failed logins) is flagged, reducing noise. They don't encrypt, compress, or synchronize logs.

questions.stem: Correlation of events from multiple systems during an investigation fails because timestamps don't line up. Which control would MOST directly prevent this?
options: Centralized time synchronization such as NTP
questions.explanation: Synchronized clocks are required to correlate events across sources. Hashing and WORM storage protect integrity, and verbosity adds detail but not consistent time.

questions.stem: An internal audit department reports to the CIO, whose systems it audits. Which is the MOST significant concern?
questions.explanation: Auditors reporting to the management they audit compromises independence and objectivity; they should report to the audit committee or board. The other issues are secondary.

questions.stem: Which metric is a key risk indicator (KRI) rather than a key performance indicator (KPI)?
options: Percentage of staff completing security training on time
Number of critical vulnerabilities older than 30 days on internet-facing systems
Mean time to close help desk tickets
Number of patches deployed per month
questions.explanation: KRIs measure exposure to risk; aging critical vulnerabilities on exposed systems signal rising risk. The others measure process performance or activity.

questions.stem: Which test verifies that a new code change did not break previously working functionality?
questions.explanation: Regression testing re-runs earlier tests after changes to catch reintroduced defects. Acceptance confirms user requirements, penetration finds exploitable flaws, and load testing measures performance.

questions.stem: During a test, defenders are not told an assessment is occurring and the testers receive only the company name. This is BEST described as:
questions.explanation: In double-blind testing neither the security staff knows of the test nor do the testers have internal information, testing detection and response. A blind test only limits tester knowledge.

questions.stem: A test plan achieves 100% statement coverage but critical defects slip through in conditional logic. Which coverage measure would BEST address this?
questions.explanation: Branch coverage ensures each true/false outcome of every decision is exercised, catching untested paths that statement coverage misses. Function and line coverage are weaker than or equal to statement coverage.

questions.stem: After a penetration test, the report to executive management should FOCUS on:
options: Raw tool output for all hosts
Business risk of findings and prioritized remediation
questions.explanation: Executives need business impact and prioritized recommendations. Technical details belong in appendices for technical teams.

questions.stem: A breach and attack simulation (BAS) platform shows endpoint controls block 95% of simulated techniques, yet a red team achieves domain admin in two days. What is the MOST likely explanation?
options: Red teams always succeed so results are meaningless
BAS validates individual controls but doesn't model adaptive, chained attacker behavior and process gaps
questions.explanation: BAS runs atomic technique checks against controls, while red teams chain techniques, adapt, and exploit identity and process weaknesses. Both are complementary; the discrepancy doesn't imply misconfiguration.

questions.stem: Which activity is MOST appropriate for testing a disaster recovery plan without disrupting operations while still exercising technical recovery?
questions.explanation: A parallel test brings up recovery systems alongside production without cutting over. Full interruption disrupts production, while checklist and read-through tests don't exercise technical recovery.

questions.stem: Which statements accurately describe a vulnerability assessment compared with a penetration test? (Select TWO.)
options: A vulnerability assessment identifies and prioritizes weaknesses without exploiting them
A vulnerability assessment always requires social engineering
A penetration test attempts to exploit weaknesses to demonstrate impact
A penetration test is fully automated and requires no human tester
A vulnerability assessment requires no authorization
questions.explanation: Vulnerability assessments find and rank weaknesses; penetration tests actively exploit them to show real impact. Penetration tests rely on skilled humans, and all testing requires authorization.

questions.stem: Which are characteristics of interactive application security testing (IAST)? (Select TWO.)
options: Uses instrumentation inside the running application
Analyzes code only when it is not running
Correlates runtime behavior with specific lines of code
Requires no test traffic to exercise the application
Replaces the need for any code review
questions.explanation: IAST agents instrument the running app and map findings to code locations, combining SAST and DAST strengths. It needs traffic to exercise code and doesn't replace review.

questions.stem: Drag the steps into the correct order for a typical penetration test methodology.
questions.explanation: Testing starts with planning and authorization, then discovery, vulnerability identification, exploitation, and finally reporting. Exploiting before authorization or discovery is improper and impractical.

questions.stem: Drag the steps into the correct order for conducting an internal security audit.
options: Issue the audit report and track remediation
questions.explanation: Audits define scope and objectives, plan procedures, collect evidence, analyze against criteria, then report and follow up. Reporting before analysis would lack supported conclusions.
